about: A Zork-style cave adventure. A Wizard has hoarded the Empire's lost treasures south of a ravine. There is a garden, a spinning Carousel Room that scrambles which way you go, a maze of oddly angled rooms, and a door guarded by a hungry lizard. The goal seems to be finding the treasures.

done.why: The lizard door wanted something with legs that crunches. I had no idea where to find it, the Carousel Room kept scrambling my movement, and I got tired of wandering.

moments.note: The Wizard appeared, made me drop the lamp, and told me where the treasure was.
I tried to take the key from the unicorn and it ran away. I didn't know that would happen.
The Carousel Room sent me in random directions, so I couldn't tell how to reach the climbing passage.
The oddly-angled rooms looped back on themselves and I couldn't map them.
I fed the teapot to the lizard before I knew what it wanted.

wished: Know what the lizard eats before I wasted the teapot.
Have a way to stop or navigate the spinning room.
Know what was nearby that I could still use.

lines.line: His eye goes to your hands, which hold nothing he values, and he relaxes a little
lines.why: The Wizard's line gave me a direction and some character.

lines.line: Visitors report a loud whirring from somewhere past the garden, as of a room that will not keep still
lines.why: The newspaper in the gazebo was funny and also a hint.

lines.line: That was not what it wanted; it ate it because it was there
lines.why: A clear refusal that told me I was on the wrong track.

fun.why: The writing was charming. I got stuck in the maze and with the lizard.

engagement.why: I wanted to solve the lizard but there was no obvious next step.

difficulty.why: The random exits and the unclear lizard puzzle were hard for a new player.

interestingness.why: The wizard, the garden, the carousel and the unicorn were all interesting.

prose.why: The prose was witty and gave useful hints.
